title: Quasipolynomial construction of a pure approximate Bayes-Nash equilibrium under independent uniform types and existence of a pure equilibrium
author: Per Austrin, Mark Braverman, and Eden Chlamtac
work: Inapproximability of NP-Complete Variants of Nash Equilibrium
source_version: Theory of Computing volume 9 article 3 (2013), official complete journal PDF acquired 2026-09-30; canonical DOI 10.4086/toc.2013.v009a003 verified against official landing and printed PDF header
difficulty_reason: After standard Chernoff-Hoeffding and polynomial-time linear programming prerequisites, the target still requires simultaneous typewise payoff guessing, compatible allowed-support constraints, a well-supported approximate Bayesian equilibrium, and purification over independently sampled type strategies with a separate small-type regime. The complete new guessing claim and LP/purification construction are at native1623–1688. This is one H2 constructive pure Bayesian-equilibrium outcome beyond routine equilibrium existence or concentration qualifications; the cited LMM mixed-equilibrium algorithm is not assumed to solve this target.

source_check.note: Exact formal Theorem6.1 only: a two-player Bayesian game whose joint type distribution is uniform on the product of equally sized type spaces, normalized payoffs in [0,1], equally sized action spaces, and an existing pure BNE admits a pure epsilon-BNE in the original n^{O((ln n+ln k)/epsilon^2)} time. Complete original Bayesian model, payoff guessing, allowed-support linear program, well-supported inequalities, sampling-to-pure closing and small-type brute-force closing are retained. The source-stated Chernoff-Hoeffding lemma is a named prerequisite, and the previous LMM algorithm is only a comparison. Hidden-clique hardness, general correlated-type hardness and small-support variants are unselected and uncounted. All-page source/output QA completed and exact final actual logs checked. Source-material candidate only; no admission/remote-delivery credit. Root admitted this exact original authored material as one H2 unit; source quirks retained unchanged.
